stories.teaser: Technion makes green hydrogen and a valuable chemical, at 98% efficiency
stories.headline: Technion researchers make green hydrogen and a valuable industrial chemical at 98% efficiency
stories.why: A membrane-free method published in Nature Communications; a US patent application has been filed.
texts:
Clean fuel, plus a bonus.

Technion researchers led by Prof. Avner Rothschild found a way to split water into green hydrogen while producing epoxide, an ingredient used in plastics, coatings and medicines, instead of plain oxygen. Both reactions ran at 98% efficiency.

“We approached this challenge by rethinking the water-splitting process,” he says.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen

98% efficiency, for two products at once.

A Technion team has developed a membrane-free method that produces green hydrogen and the industrial chemical epoxide together, with only 2% of the electrical charge lost to other reactions. The researchers say the current density is compatible with large-scale industrial electrolysis. Published in Nature Communications.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen

What if making clean fuel also made something valuable on the side?

That’s the idea behind a new Technion method that turns water and renewable electricity into green hydrogen and epoxide, a building block for polymers, adhesives and pharmaceuticals.

“By optimizing the entire system, we succeeded in producing both hydrogen and epoxide efficiently,” says Dr. Guilin Ruan.

#Israel #Technion #CleanEnergy #Hydrogen
stories.og_title: Technion develops breakthrough method to produce green hydrogen and epoxide

stories.headline: A 300-meter stretch of Jerusalem’s 2,000-year-old aqueduct is uncovered
stories.why: The Lower Aqueduct carried water about 21 km to the Temple Mount; it will be displayed in a new neighborhood.
texts:
2,000 years ago, Jerusalem got its water by gravity alone.

The Israel Antiquities Authority has uncovered a 300-meter stretch of the Lower Aqueduct in southern Jerusalem. The channel dropped only about one meter per kilometer on its roughly 21 km route to the Temple Mount.

“The aqueduct is an engineering marvel,” says IAA Jerusalem District Archaeologist Amit Re’em.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History

300 meters uncovered. About 21 km long. Around 2,000 years old.

The Israel Antiquities Authority has exposed a section of Jerusalem’s Lower Aqueduct, which brought spring water to the Temple Mount. It was used on and off until about 100 years ago. Planners want to display the remains along a promenade in a new neighborhood.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History

How did ancient Jerusalem get its water?

Through an aqueduct so gently sloped it dropped about one meter per kilometer. A 300-meter stretch has just been uncovered.

“The thought that about 2,000 years ago they managed to bring water to Jerusalem this way is astonishing,” says IAA archaeologist Amit Re’em.

#Israel #Archaeology #Jerusalem #History
stories.og_title: 300-meter stretch of ancient aqueduct uncovered during planning for new Jerusalem neighborhood

stories.teaser: New Israel Museum show explores childhood in ancient Israel
stories.headline: New Israel Museum exhibition explores childhood in the ancient Land of Israel
stories.why: “Tiny Footprints” brings together hundreds of artifacts from 11 institutions, from prehistory to the first millennium CE.
texts:
What was it like to be a child 3,000 years ago?

The Israel Museum’s new exhibition, “Tiny Footprints: Childhood in the Ancient Land of Israel,” gathers hundreds of artifacts from 11 institutions: a 3,000-year-old pottery pull toy shaped like an otter, tiny hand axes sized for small hands, and figurines carrying a child’s fingerprints.

“Mothers are mothers wherever they are, and children act like children,” says curator Tali Sharvit.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture

Hundreds of artifacts. 11 institutions. Thousands of years of childhood.

“Tiny Footprints” at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem traces children’s lives from prehistory to the end of the first millennium CE, with toys, feeding vessels, a Byzantine writing tablet and a mosaic of a boy in a short tunic. It runs through the end of February.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture

Did ancient kids play with toys like ours?

They did. A new exhibition at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem shows a pottery otter on wheels from the 11th century BCE and much more.

“What’s amazing about these toys is how similar they are to today,” says curator Tali Sharvit.

#Israel #IsraelMuseum #Archaeology #Culture
stories.og_title: From birth to play, new exhibition explores childhood in ancient Israel

stories.teaser: Israeli scientists find how cancer cells survive chemotherapy
stories.headline: Ben-Gurion University scientists find ‘guardian proteins’ that help cancer cells survive chemo
stories.why: Dr. Aeid Igbaria’s lab identified two proteins, DNAJB12 and DNAJB14, in a study published in Redox Biology.
texts:
Why do some cancers survive chemotherapy? Israeli scientists may have found part of the answer.

Dr. Aeid Igbaria’s lab at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev identified two “guardian proteins” that open an emergency valve, letting cancer cells survive the stress of treatment. When the bonds holding them together break, the guardians fall apart, clearing the way for the cancer cell to self-destruct.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU

2 proteins. 1 emergency valve that keeps cancer cells alive.

Researchers at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev found that the proteins DNAJB12 and DNAJB14 help cancer cells survive chemotherapy stress. The work, done in human cell lines and published in Redox Biology, offers a new target for tackling chemo resistance.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU

Cancer plays chess. Now scientists know one of its moves.

“When we talk about cancer, it’s like we are talking about playing chess,” says Dr. Aeid Igbaria of Ben-Gurion University. His lab found two “guardian proteins” that help cancer cells survive chemotherapy, research that may help future treatments overcome resistance.

#Israel #Science #CancerResearch #BGU
stories.og_title: How cancer cells survive chemo: Israeli researchers find 'guardian proteins' protect tumors

stories.teaser: Raz Hershko wins bronze at the World Judo Championships
stories.headline: Israel’s Raz Hershko wins bronze at the World Judo Championships
stories.why: In Baku, the +78 kg judoka won four bouts, including the bronze match by ippon in golden score.
texts:
Another world medal for Israel.

Judoka Raz Hershko won bronze in the +78 kg category at the World Judo Championships in Baku. After wins over opponents from Chinese Taipei, Estonia and Brazil, she clinched the medal by ippon against Croatia’s Helena Vuković in golden score.

Proud of her.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael

4 wins. 1 world bronze.

Israel’s Raz Hershko took bronze in the women’s +78 kg division at the World Judo Championships in Baku, beating Croatia’s Helena Vuković by ippon in golden score in the bronze-medal bout. Earlier she defeated opponents from Chinese Taipei, Estonia and Brazil.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael

What does it take to win a world medal in golden score?

Ask Raz Hershko. After four minutes of regulation time, the Israeli judoka beat Croatia’s Helena Vuković by ippon in golden score to win bronze at the World Judo Championships in Baku. It was her fourth win of the tournament in the +78 kg category.

#Israel #Judo #Sport #TeamIsrael
stories.og_title: Raz Hershko Wins Bronze Medal at the World Judo Championships

stories.teaser: Weizmann AI rebuilds what you see from a brain scan
stories.headline: Weizmann Institute AI reconstructs what people see from their brain scans
stories.why: Brain-IT adapts to a new person with about one hour of scan data, instead of the 40 hours earlier methods needed.
texts:
Imagine a computer drawing the picture you’re looking at, just from your brain activity.

A team led by Prof. Michal Irani at Israel’s Weizmann Institute built Brain-IT, an AI that reconstructs images people view from fMRI scans. It needs only about one hour of scan data from a new person, instead of 40. One day, it could help paralyzed people communicate.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience

40 hours of brain scans, cut to about 1.

The Weizmann Institute’s Brain-IT system reconstructs the images people look at from fMRI brain scans, and adapts to a new person with about an hour of data. On data from four volunteers, it outperformed 10 other methods on 7 of 8 standard image-similarity measures. Presented at ICLR 2026.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience

Can AI see what you see?

Researchers at Israel’s Weizmann Institute, led by Prof. Michal Irani, built a system that turns brain scans into pictures of what a person is viewing. It is especially good at capturing layout, color and shape, and needs far less data than earlier methods.

#Israel #Science #AI #Neuroscience
stories.og_title: This AI Reconstructs What You're Looking at From a Brain Scan
